Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A method, device and system for detecting and counteracting a runaway condition in a diesel engine system. The diesel engine system includes an inlet for supplying combustion air to a diesel engine, and an exhaust for relieving the diesel engine from exhaust gas. The diesel engine system further includes an exhaust gas recirculation system for selectively allowing exhaust gas from the exhaust to enter the inlet. A first gas flow path actuator is included in the exhaust gas recirculation system, and a second gas flow path actuator is included in the exhaust. The method, as performed by the system, comprises detection of an actual or potential runaway condition, and in response thereto deprives the diesel engine of oxygen. Depriving of oxygen is performed by opening the first gas flow path actuator and closing the second gas flow path actuator to cause stalling of the diesel engine. The depriving is accomplished by maximizing recirculation of exhaust gasses to the engine and increasing pressure drop over the exhaust for a first predetermined period of time.

outputs.L1:
A method, device, and system are provided for detecting and counteracting a runaway condition in a diesel engine system. The diesel engine system includes an inlet for supplying combustion air to a diesel engine and an exhaust for discharging exhaust gas from the engine. The system further includes an exhaust gas recirculation system configured to selectively direct exhaust gas from the exhaust into the inlet. A first gas-flow-path actuator is provided in the exhaust gas recirculation system, and a second gas-flow-path actuator is provided in the exhaust.

The method, as performed by the system, comprises detecting an actual or potential runaway condition and, in response, depriving the diesel engine of oxygen. This oxygen deprivation is achieved by opening the first gas-flow-path actuator and closing the second gas-flow-path actuator, thereby causing the diesel engine to stall. More specifically, oxygen deprivation is accomplished by maximizing exhaust gas recirculation to the engine and increasing the pressure drop across the exhaust for a first predetermined period of time.
outputs.L2: Disclosed are a method, apparatus, and system for identifying and suppressing an actual or impending runaway event in a diesel engine arrangement. The arrangement has an intake that delivers combustion air to the diesel engine and an exhaust passage that removes exhaust gases from it. It also incorporates an exhaust-gas recirculation system configured to selectively route gases from the exhaust passage back into the intake. A first gas-flow actuator is positioned within the recirculation system, while a second gas-flow actuator is located in the exhaust passage. When the system detects a present or potential runaway condition, it responds by cutting off the engine’s oxygen supply. This is achieved by opening the first actuator and shutting the second actuator, thereby causing the diesel engine to stall. For a first predefined time interval, exhaust-gas recirculation to the engine is maximized and the pressure drop across the exhaust is increased to produce the oxygen-depriving effect.
outputs.L3:
The disclosed method, device, and system are designed to detect and counteract an actual or potential runaway condition in a diesel engine. The diesel engine system includes a combustion-air inlet, an exhaust outlet, and an exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system that routes exhaust gas from the exhaust outlet back to the combustion-air inlet.

A first gas-flow actuator regulates the recirculation of exhaust gas through the EGR system, while a second gas-flow actuator controls the flow of exhaust gas through the exhaust outlet. When an actual or potential runaway condition is detected, the system opens the first actuator to maximize exhaust gas recirculation and closes the second actuator to restrict exhaust flow. These actions increase the pressure drop across the exhaust system and direct a greater proportion of exhaust gas back into the combustion-air inlet.

The resulting increase in recirculated exhaust gas reduces the amount of oxygen available for combustion. By maintaining this condition for a predetermined period, the system deprives the engine of sufficient oxygen to continue operating, causing it to stall and thereby stopping the runaway condition.
outputs.L4:
A method, device, and system are provided for detecting and suppressing an actual or potential runaway condition in a diesel engine. The system includes an electronic controller that receives operating data from one or more sensors, such as engine-speed, accelerator-position, fuel-delivery, intake-pressure, exhaust-pressure, airflow, and temperature sensors. Based on these data, the controller determines whether the engine is accelerating or operating independently of the commanded fuel input. A runaway condition may be identified, for example, when engine speed exceeds a predetermined threshold, increases at an abnormal rate, or remains elevated after commanded fuel delivery has been reduced or stopped.

When a runaway condition is detected, the controller initiates an emergency shutdown sequence. Fuel delivery may first be reduced or discontinued. Because a diesel engine can continue operating by consuming an unintended fuel source, however, interruption of the normal fuel supply may not be sufficient. The controller therefore commands an exhaust-gas recirculation actuator toward an open position while commanding an exhaust-path actuator toward a closed or restricted position. The exhaust-gas recirculation actuator may be an EGR valve, and the exhaust-path actuator may be an exhaust throttle, brake valve, flap, or other flow-restricting device located downstream of the EGR takeoff.

Opening the EGR valve and restricting the exhaust path create a pressure differential that drives a large quantity of exhaust gas back into the engine intake. The recirculated gas displaces fresh air and reduces the concentration and mass flow of oxygen available for combustion. At the same time, restriction of the exhaust path increases exhaust backpressure and the pumping work required from the engine. The combined reduction in intake oxygen and increase in exhaust resistance suppress combustion, decelerate the engine, and ultimately cause it to stall.

The actuators may be maintained in their commanded positions for a predetermined interval or until sensor information confirms that engine speed has fallen below a shutdown threshold. The controller may then keep the engine in a disabled state, gradually return the actuators to their normal positions, or require a manual reset before restarting is permitted. Diagnostic information concerning the event may also be stored and communicated to an operator, service tool, or remote monitoring system.

The method can be implemented in engine-control software, in a separate runaway-protection controller, or through coordinated operation of multiple vehicle or machine controllers. It may be used with turbocharged or naturally aspirated diesel engines and can supplement conventional fuel shutoff and intake-air shutdown mechanisms. By maximizing exhaust-gas recirculation and increasing the exhaust pressure drop for a controlled period, the system provides a rapid means of depriving the engine of oxygen, thereby stalling the engine and preventing or limiting an uncontrolled overspeed event.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a method and system that detects diesel engine runaway and stops the engine by maximizing exhaust gas recirculation and restricting exhaust flow.
counterfactuals.output: A method and system for controlling a diesel engine during a runaway condition are disclosed. An electronic controller receives one or more operating parameters, including engine speed, commanded fueling, intake pressure, exhaust pressure, and accelerator demand, and detects the runaway condition when the operating parameters satisfy a predetermined criterion, such as engine speed exceeding a threshold independently of commanded fueling. In response, the controller commands an exhaust gas recirculation valve toward a maximum-flow position and actuates an exhaust-flow restriction device toward a restricted position. The resulting exhaust backpressure increases recirculated exhaust gas and reduces the oxygen concentration of the intake charge, thereby suppressing combustion of fuel or other combustible material entering the engine independently of the normal fuel-delivery system. The controller may additionally discontinue commanded fuel injection and regulate the exhaust-flow restriction to maintain pressure within allowable limits. The coordinated increase in exhaust gas recirculation and restriction of exhaust flow decelerates and stops the engine while reducing the likelihood of mechanical damage.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention that uses EGR and exhaust actuators to detect and counteract an actual or potential runaway condition in a diesel engine.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention provides a control system for preventing or stopping diesel-engine runaway. An engine controller monitors operating parameters—such as engine speed, acceleration, fueling commands, intake airflow, or exhaust conditions—to identify an actual runaway or predict that one is developing.

When a runaway condition is detected, the controller operates the exhaust-gas recirculation (EGR) system and one or more exhaust actuators, such as an exhaust throttle, backpressure valve, or variable-geometry turbocharger. These actions increase exhaust backpressure, recirculate more oxygen-depleted exhaust gas, and reduce the fresh air available for combustion. The resulting reduction in oxygen and engine torque slows or shuts down the engine, including when unintended fuel or combustible vapors are entering independently of the normal fuel-injection system. The actuators may be applied individually or in a coordinated sequence, with diagnostic and reset logic to avoid unnecessary intervention.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical description of a diesel engine safety system that deprives the engine of oxygen by opening an exhaust gas recirculation valve and closing an exhaust valve for a predetermined period.
counterfactuals.output:
### Diesel Engine Oxygen-Deprivation Safety System

The safety system is configured to shut down a diesel engine, including during an uncontrolled or “runaway” operating condition, by reducing the oxygen concentration of the engine intake charge. The system includes an exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) passage connecting the engine exhaust system to the intake system, a controllable EGR valve disposed in the EGR passage, and a controllable exhaust shutoff valve positioned in the exhaust conduit downstream of the EGR passage takeoff.

An electronic safety controller receives one or more engine operating signals, such as engine speed, commanded fueling, oil pressure, intake pressure, or a manual emergency-stop input. When a shutdown condition is detected, the controller commands the EGR valve to an open position and commands the exhaust shutoff valve to a closed or substantially closed position. Closing the exhaust shutoff valve increases exhaust-system backpressure and directs exhaust gas through the open EGR passage into the intake system. The recirculated exhaust gas displaces oxygen-containing fresh air, thereby reducing the oxygen concentration available for combustion. Once the intake oxygen concentration falls below that required to sustain combustion, engine torque decreases and the engine stops.

The EGR valve and exhaust shutoff valve are maintained in their shutdown positions for a predetermined period selected to ensure that combustion has ceased and that residual rotational energy has dissipated. The period may be fixed or may be supplemented by confirmation that engine speed has fallen below a specified threshold. After expiration of the period and confirmation of shutdown, the controller may reopen the exhaust shutoff valve and return the EGR valve to its normal position to relieve trapped exhaust pressure and permit servicing or a controlled restart.

The system may operate independently of the normal fuel-shutoff system or in conjunction with a command that terminates fuel injection. Position sensors, exhaust- and intake-pressure sensors, and diagnostic logic may be provided to verify valve actuation, detect excessive pressure, and prevent restart until the safety system has been reset. Components exposed to elevated exhaust pressure and temperature are rated accordingly, and pressure-relief or bypass provisions may be included to protect the engine and exhaust system from overpressure.

counterfactuals.output: A diesel engine runaway prevention system includes a controller configured to detect an engine runaway condition based on one or more operating parameters, including engine speed, acceleration, fueling command, intake pressure, or exhaust pressure. Upon detecting the runaway condition, the controller actuates an exhaust restriction device to increase exhaust backpressure and commands an exhaust gas recirculation system to maximize recirculated exhaust gas flow to the engine intake. The increased exhaust backpressure and recirculated exhaust gas reduce the availability of oxygen for combustion and increase engine pumping resistance, thereby reducing engine torque and stalling the engine. The system may independently control an exhaust brake, variable-geometry turbocharger, exhaust throttle, recirculation valve, or combinations thereof, and may initiate the shutdown response independently of a normal engine fueling command. Related control methods and engine systems are also disclosed.
